# Functions

## Population Sampler
### Creates a stratified population based on designated sample size so we are able to have representation for all counties.
```{r}
stratified_sample_picker = function(df, s){
  
  fraction = s / nrow(df)
  
  sampled_data = df %>% 
    group_by(in.county) %>% 
    sample_frac(fraction)

  return(sampled_data)
}


```

## House Energy Picker
### Lets you pick the correct house energy file. Will return the file as a dataframe.
```{r}
house_energy_picker = function(identifier){
  
  tempFileStart = "https://intro-datascience.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/SC-data/2023-houseData/"
  tempFilePicked = identifier
  tempFileEnd = ".parquet"
  
  tempDF = read_parquet(paste0(tempFileStart, tempFilePicked, tempFileEnd))
  tempDF$time = as.POSIXct(tempDF$time)

  tempDF = tempDF %>% 
    filter(time >= as.POSIXct("2018-07-01 00:00:00") & time <= as.POSIXct("2018-07-31 23:00:00"))  
  
  return(tempDF)
}

```

## House Weather Picker
### Lets you pick the correct house weather file. Will return the file as a dataframe.
```{r}
house_weather_picker = function(countyCode){
  
  tempFileStart = "https://intro-datascience.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/SC-data/weather/2023-weather-data/"
  tempFilePicked = countyCode
  tempFileEnd = ".csv"
  
  tempDF = read_csv(paste0(tempFileStart, tempFilePicked, tempFileEnd), show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  tempDF = tempDF %>%
    rename(time = date_time)
  
  tempDF$time = as.POSIXct(tempDF$time)
  
  tempDF = tempDF %>% 
    filter(time >= as.POSIXct("2018-07-01 00:00:00") & time <= as.POSIXct("2018-07-31 23:00:00"))
  
  # For merging
  tempDF$in.county = countyCode
  
  return(tempDF)
}

```

## Process Sampler
### Takes the dataframes of house and house energy usage and merges them together. For July
```{r}
process_sample = function(sampled_df) {
  
  # Download weather per county
  counties_needed = unique(sampled_df$in.county)
  weather_list = list()
  
  for (county in counties_needed) {
    weather_list[[county]] = house_weather_picker(county)
  }
  
  all_weather = bind_rows(weather_list)
  
  #Download energy for each house
  house_ids = sampled_df$bldg_id
  energy_list = list()
  
  for (i in seq_along(house_ids)) {
    energy_df = house_energy_picker(house_ids[i])
    energy_df$bldg_id = house_ids[i]
    energy_list[[i]] = energy_df
  }
  
  all_energy = bind_rows(energy_list)
  
  # Add county to energy for joining
  house_county_map = sampled_df %>% 
    select(bldg_id, in.county)
  
  all_energy = all_energy %>% 
    left_join(house_county_map, by = "bldg_id")
  
  # Join energy + weather
  merged_E_W = all_energy %>% 
    left_join(all_weather, by = c("in.county", "time"))
  
  # Join with house static data
  combined_df = merged_E_W %>% 
    left_join(house_static_df, by = c("bldg_id", "in.county"))
  
  return(combined_df)
}

```

## Find missing values
### Find values in data that aren't in ordering
```{r}
find_missing_levels = function(df, col_name, expected_levels) {
  actual_values = unique(df[[col_name]])
  missing = setdiff(actual_values, expected_levels)
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    print(paste("\n", col_name, " - VALUES IN DATA NOT IN YOUR ORDERING:\n", sep = ""))
    print(missing)
  }
}
```

## Dictionary Lookup
### Takes the attribute name, looks in the metadata and returns the field_name, field_description, allowable_enumerations_baseline.
```{r}
dic_lookup = function(name){
  
  md_ID_df %>% 
    select(field_name, field_description, allowable_enumerations_baseline) %>% 
    filter(field_name == name)
  
}
```

## Calculate interaction terms
### Give the name of the new dataframe and automatically calculate the interaction terms.
```{r}
interaction_calc = function(df){
    # Calculate interaction terms
    df$temp_x_insulation_wall = df$`Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * df$in.insulation_wall
    df$temp_x_insulation_ceiling = df$`Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * df$in.insulation_ceiling
    df$temp_x_hvac = df$`Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * df$in.hvac_cooling_efficiency
    df$temp_x_windows = df$`Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * df$in.windows
    df$temp_x_window_area = df$`Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * df$in.window_areas
    df$hour_x_temp = df$hour * df$`Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]`
    df$temp_x_humidity = df$`Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * df$`Relative Humidity [%]`
    df$solar_x_windows = df$`Global Horizontal Radiation [W/m2]` * df$in.windows
    df$solar_x_window_area = df$`Global Horizontal Radiation [W/m2]` * df$in.window_areas
    
    return(df)
}

```

## Confirming NA's
```{r}
# Find NA
check_factor_nas = function(df, col_name) {
  na_count = sum(is.na(df[[col_name]]))
  total = nrow(df)
  pct = round(na_count / total * 100, 2)
  cat(col_name, ": ", na_count, " NAs (", pct, "%)\n", sep = "")
}
```

## Model 1
### Adjusted R-Value 0.21507007
```{r}
# Base model to try
lmModel = lm(usage_per_sqft ~ .- in.county, data = modelDF)

# Base model with only significant values
lmModel_base_only_sig = lm(usage_per_sqft ~ . - in.county - day_of_week, data = modelDF)

# Base model with only insulation
lmModel_insulation = lm(usage_per_sqft ~ `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]`+
                          `Global Horizontal Radiation [W/m2]` +
                          `Relative Humidity [%]` + 
                          in.insulation_ceiling+
                          in.insulation_floor+
                          in.insulation_foundation_wall+
                          in.insulation_wall+
                          in.insulation_slab, data = modelDF)

# Base model with insulation and house size
lmModel_house_size = lm(usage_per_sqft ~ `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]`+
                          `Global Horizontal Radiation [W/m2]` +
                          `Relative Humidity [%]` + 
                          in.insulation_ceiling+
                          in.insulation_floor+
                          in.insulation_foundation_wall+
                          in.insulation_wall+
                          in.insulation_slab+
                          in.bedrooms+
                          in.geometry_stories+
                          in.occupants, data = modelDF,)

# Put into a dataframe to compare it
model_comparison = data.frame(
  Model = c("lmModel", "lmModel_base_only_sig", "lmModel_insulation", "lmModel_house_size"),
  R_Squared = c(
    summary(lmModel)$r.squared,
    summary(lmModel_base_only_sig)$r.squared,
    summary(lmModel_insulation)$r.squared,
    summary(lmModel_house_size)$r.squared
  ),
  Adj_R_Squared = c(
    summary(lmModel)$adj.r.squared,
    summary(lmModel_base_only_sig)$adj.r.squared,
    summary(lmModel_insulation)$adj.r.squared,
    summary(lmModel_house_size)$adj.r.squared
  ),
  Num_Predictors = c(
    length(coef(lmModel)) - 1,
    length(coef(lmModel_base_only_sig)) - 1,
    length(coef(lmModel_insulation)) - 1,
    length(coef(lmModel_house_size)) - 1
  )
)
# Sort by best first
model_comparison = model_comparison %>% arrange(desc(Adj_R_Squared))
print(model_comparison)

```

```{r}
library(caret)

train_indices = createDataPartition(
  modelDF_interaction$total_usage, 
  p = 0.80, 
  list = FALSE
)

train_df = modelDF_interaction[train_indices, ]
test_df = modelDF_interaction[-train_indices, ]

dim(modelDF_interaction)
dim(train_df)
dim(test_df)


lm_with_interactions = lm(total_usage ~ . - in.county - bldg_id, 
  data = train_df
)

test_df$predicted = predict(lm_with_interactions, newdata = test_df)
rmse = sqrt(mean((test_df$total_usage - test_df$predicted)^2))
mae = mean(abs(test_df$total_usage - test_df$predicted))
print(paste("Test RMSE:", rmse, "Test MAE:", mae))
```

```{r}
  in.geometry_stories = 2,
  
  # Factor/character variables
  in.occupants = "3",                          
  in.cooling_setpoint = "72F",
  in.infiltration = "5 ACH50",
  in.orientation = "South",                   
  in.roof_material = "Asphalt Shingles, Medium",
  in.vintage = "1990s",
  in.geometry_garage = "2 Car",
  
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Calculate interaction terms
new_data = interaction_calc(new_data)

# Predict
predicted_usage = predict(lm_with_interactions, newdata = new_data)
print(paste("Predicted usage:", predicted_usage, "kWh"))
```

## +5 Perdictor
```{r}
future_df = modelDF_interaction %>%
  mutate(
    `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` = `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` + 5,
    temp_x_insulation_wall = `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * in.insulation_wall,
    temp_x_insulation_ceiling = `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * in.insulation_ceiling,
    temp_x_hvac = `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * in.hvac_cooling_efficiency,
    temp_x_windows = `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * in.windows,
    temp_x_window_area = `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * in.window_areas,
    hour_x_temp = hour * `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]`,
    temp_x_humidity = `Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]` * `Relative Humidity [%]`
  )

future_df$predicted_usage = predict(lm_with_interactions, newdata = future_df)

modelDF_interaction$predicted_usage = predict(lm_with_interactions, newdata = modelDF_interaction)

# Compare current vs future by hour
current_hourly = modelDF_interaction %>%
  group_by(hour) %>%
  summarise(
    total_demand = sum(predicted_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_demand = mean(predicted_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(scenario = "Current")

future_hourly = future_df %>%
  group_by(hour) %>%
  summarise(
    total_demand = sum(predicted_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_demand = mean(predicted_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(scenario = "Future (+5°C)")

# Combine for comparison
comparison_hourly = bind_rows(current_hourly, future_hourly)

# Find peak demand
cat("\n=== PEAK DEMAND COMPARISON ===\n")
current_peak = current_hourly %>% slice_max(total_demand, n = 1)
future_peak = future_hourly %>% slice_max(total_demand, n = 1)

cat("Current Peak Hour:", current_peak$hour, ":00\n")
cat("Current Peak Demand:", round(current_peak$total_demand, 2), "kWh\n")
cat("\nFuture Peak Hour:", future_peak$hour, ":00\n")
cat("Future Peak Demand:", round(future_peak$total_demand, 2), "kWh\n")

cat("\n=== INCREASE ===\n")
demand_increase = future_peak$total_demand - current_peak$total_demand
pct_increase = (demand_increase / current_peak$total_demand) * 100
cat("Absolute Increase:", round(demand_increase, 2), "kWh\n")
cat("Percent Increase:", round(pct_increase, 2), "%\n")

# Visualize
ggplot(comparison_hourly, aes(x = hour, y = total_demand, color = scenario)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Current" = "steelblue", "Future (+5°C)" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "Current vs Future Peak Demand by Hour",
    subtitle = "Impact of 5°C temperature increase on total energy demand",
    x = "Hour of Day",
    y = "Total Predicted Demand (kWh)",
    color = "Scenario"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 2)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

```{r}
                                "Double/Triple Low-E (8-11)" = "green")) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Homes by Window Type",
    subtitle = "Number of houses in each window category",
    x = "Window Type Category",
    y = "Number of Houses"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  ylim(0, max(window_distribution$n_houses) * 1.15)

print(graph_window_dist)

```

```{r}
# Window Type Distribution by Home Size

window_by_size = future_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(window_category) & !is.na(size_category)) %>%
  group_by(size_category, window_category) %>%
  summarise(
    n_houses = n_distinct(bldg_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(size_category) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = round(n_houses / sum(n_houses) * 100, 1)
  )

graph_window_by_size = ggplot(window_by_size, aes(x = size_category, y = n_houses, fill = window_category)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
```
